claim: Google LLC v. Oracle America, Inc., 593 U.S. 1 (2021), decided April 5, 2021, in a 6–2 opinion by Justice Breyer, held that Google's copying of approximately 11,500 lines of declaring code was fair use as a matter of law.
evidence: Held: Google's copying of the Java SE API, which included only those lines of code that were needed to allow programmers to put their accrued talents to work in a new and transformative program, was a fair use of that material as a matter of law.
excerpt:
Argued October 7, 2020—Decided April 5, 2021 Oracle America, Inc., owns a copyright in Java SE, a computer platform that uses the popular Java computer programming language. In 2005, Google acquired Android and sought to build a new software platform for mobile devices. To allow the millions of programmers familiar with the Java programming language to work with its new Android plat - form, Google copied roughly 11,500 lines of code from the Java SE pro - gram.
